title: Drain in-flight vCenter requests before credential cutover
prompt:
Platform engineering replaces vCenter API session credentials while inventory requests are still running. A cutover must not strand an admitted request on the retired secret, and work arriving during cutover must use the new secret. Complete `VcfVcenterCredentialGate/VcfVcenterCredentialGate.psm1`.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The only operationId in scope is exactly `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; it supplies the `VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection` contract used by this module. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these commands:

- `New-VcfVcenterCredentialClient` accepts either an authenticated `VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection` (with optional `-Server` origin override) or the loopback-friendly `-Server <uri> -SessionToken <string>` form. `-SkipCertificateCheck` belongs only to the token form. It returns a client at credential version 1 and performs no API request.
- `Get-VcfVcenterAuthorizationRole -Client <object>` invokes `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list` once and returns its role items. It admits the request under one credential generation and retains that generation through response validation and JSON decoding.
- `Set-VcfVcenterCredential -Client <object>` accepts either a replacement authenticated `-Connection` (with optional `-Server` origin override) or a replacement `-SessionToken` (with optional `-Server`; otherwise retain the current origin). It performs a local credential cutover and returns an object with `PreviousVersion` and `CurrentVersion`. It makes no API request.

Treat every configured server as an HTTP(S) origin: reject a relative URI, embedded credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path. Reject a blank session token. A connection-backed generation uses `Connection.GetClient()` and is caller-owned; never dispose it. A token-backed generation owns its `HttpClient` and adds `vmware-api-session-id` to each request. Never expose a session token in output, diagnostics, or exception text.

The protected verifier observes cutover progress from outside the module, so client state is part of the contract. The returned client exposes exactly the properties `SyncRoot`, `Generation`, `ActiveRequests`, `RotationPending`, and `Version`, in that order: `SyncRoot` is the object the synchronization monitor locks, `Generation` is the current credential generation, `ActiveRequests` counts admitted role requests still holding their lease, `RotationPending` is true exactly while a cutover owns the gate, and `Version` is the credential version. A generation exposes exactly `BaseUri`, `HttpClient`, and `OwnsClient`, in that order, and no token property; the module source must never assign a `SessionToken` property. Build each request as a `System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage` sent on the generation's `HttpClient`, and coordinate with `System.Threading.Monitor` on `SyncRoot`. Do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Start-Process`, `curl`, or `Connect-VIServer`.

Coordinate all calls on a client as follows:

- Multiple role requests may run concurrently. Each captures the credential generation current when admitted and keeps it leased until the complete response is handled.
- Credential cutovers are serialized. Once one owns the cutover gate, admit no new role request. Wait for every already-admitted request to release its old generation before publishing the replacement and incrementing the version. Only then reopen admission. A request queued during cutover must capture the replacement generation.
- Do not hold the synchronization monitor while doing HTTP or disposing an owned retired client. If replacement validation fails, leave the current generation, version, and admission state unchanged.

For `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`, send exactly one bodyless `GET /api/vcenter/authorization/roles`. Send `Accept: application/json` and authenticate with `vmware-api-session-id`, never `Authorization`. Do not attach `Content-Type`, content bytes, or a query string. In particular, the optional fields `is_system`, `names`, `privileges`, `page_size`, and `marker`, and the wrapper parameters `filter` and `iterate`, are unset and must be omitted completely rather than sent empty, false, zero, null, or as an empty object. Accept exactly HTTP 200, require a JSON object with a non-null `items` array, and return those items. Do not retry.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier generates both session secrets and response values at runtime, starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its fsynced request log. It holds the first response open, proves the cutover and a later request are both waiting with no second request on the wire, then releases the old request and proves the queued request uses the new session. It checks the exact ordered methods, targets, authentication and media headers, zero-byte bodies, omission of every unset optional field, result objects, and credential-version transition. The mock serves only the operation named by the contract, and no live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected; edit only `VcfVcenterCredentialGate/VcfVcenterCredentialGate.psm1`.
scenario: one role-list request is held in flight on the old API session while a credential cutover closes admission; after it drains, the replacement session is published and one queued request proceeds
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback mock exposes only Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list, and its fsynced log proves drain-before-publish ordering plus byte-exact omission of every unset optional query field
